# Eavesy

> Eavesy is a local, AI-first assistant for your Mac (Apple Silicon). You drop things into it (text or images from your clipboard, screenshots, dictation, and recordings) and it turns them into clean, structured Markdown context that is quick to copy into any AI agent or reach over MCP. It is local-first: files live on your disk as Markdown and JSON.

Meeting recording is one capability, not the headline. Eavesy is free; everyone gets the same fair-use limits: https://eavesy.com/docs/fair-use-limits

## What you can drop in (shipping today)
- Clipboard text or an image: open the launcher (global hotkey), press Cmd+V. Saved as a note (`note.md`) or `image.png`.
- Screenshots: from the launcher (macOS 14+).
- Dictation: speak, get cleaned-up text with a transcript (requires signing in).
- Recordings: screen, system audio, and microphone on the Mac app, or microphone/screen in the browser recorder. Get a transcript and a Markdown summary (title, TL;DR, decisions, action items); transcription requires signing in. Browser-recorder sessions live in the web app, not on disk. No bot joins calls.

Not available yet: forwarding messages or orders straight from other apps, live captions, reading text out of screenshots in the Mac app, and cross-device drops. Do not assume these exist.

## Where the files live
The Mac app (not the browser recorder) writes each capture to a folder under `~/Eavesy/Recordings/` (change it with Settings > Recordings folder in the launcher):

```text
~/Eavesy/Recordings/2026-06-15 Design review/
├── summary.md       # structured brief (recordings)
├── transcript.md    # full transcript
├── notes.md         # the user's own notes
├── meeting.json     # metadata (id, title, date, durationSeconds, files)
├── audio.m4a
└── screen.mp4       # when screen capture was on
```

Clipboard and screenshot captures hold `note.md` / `image.png` / `screenshot.png` plus `capture.json`. All formats are open; read them directly with filesystem access, no API needed. Format: https://eavesy.com/docs/session-folder-format

## Connect over MCP
Server: `https://mcp.eavesy.com` (streamable HTTP). Add it by URL: the server supports MCP authorization (OAuth 2.1, PKCE, dynamic client registration, metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`), so clients like Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code send the user to sign in to Eavesy and approve the connection. No token to paste.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http eavesy https://mcp.eavesy.com
```

Or the Claude Code plugin (adds the server plus a skill for when to use it): `/plugin marketplace add williamrogersdev/eavesy`, then `/plugin install eavesy@eavesy`.

Scopes: `read` (default) and `write`. The user grants write only by ticking "Also let it write" on the approval page (or "Allow writes" for a pasted token). Tools a connection's scopes don't cover are hidden from `tools/list` and refused if called.

Fallback for clients without OAuth: create a connection in the web app under Settings > AI assistants (MCP); the token is shown once. Send it in the Authorization header. Tokens expire 90 days after last use. URL-path tokens (`https://mcp.eavesy.com/<token>`) are deprecated and work only while the server flag `MCP_ALLOW_PATH_TOKENS` is not `false`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "eavesy": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.eavesy.com",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

Tools, all read-only (names say "meeting" because that is the recording type in the data model):
- `search_meetings` (query, limit): search recordings by title or transcript; returns excerpts.
- `get_meeting` (id): summary and full transcript.
- `recent_meetings` (limit): newest recordings.
- `search_dictations` (query, limit): search dictations.
- `get_action_items` (status: open|completed|all, owner): action items across recordings.

Clipboard notes, images, and screenshots are never uploaded (they stay on the Mac), so they are not available over MCP. Docs: https://eavesy.com/docs/connect-mcp

## Copy-paste examples
Paste into an agent after copying a summary from Eavesy:

```text
Here is the context from my call (Markdown below). Draft the follow-up tasks as a checklist.
<paste summary.md>
```

Ask an MCP-connected agent:

```text
Use Eavesy to find the recording where we discussed the pricing change, then list the open action items.
```

Point a coding agent at the folder:

```bash
grep -ril "pricing" ~/Eavesy/Recordings/*/transcript.md
```

## Bring your own keys
In the web app Settings you can connect your own OpenRouter account so AI usage runs on your credits. Otherwise the hosted service handles transcription and summaries.
